name: LUTEINIZING HORMONE
description: Luteinizing Hormone (LH) measures pituitary gonadotropin function and evaluates reproductive endocrine status. This test assesses ovulation, menopause, hypogonadism, and pituitary disorders affecting LH secretion.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is a pituitary gonadotropin essential for reproductive function. In women, levels vary by menstrual cycle phase: follicular 1.7-12 mIU/mL, ovulatory surge up to 100 mIU/mL, luteal 0.6-16 mIU/mL. In men, normal range is 1.5-9.3 mIU/mL. Elevated LH suggests primary gonadal failure, menopause, or pituitary tumors. Low LH indicates pituitary insufficiency or hypothalamic dysfunction. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides excellent sensitivity. LH:FSH ratio helps differentiate polycystic ovary syndrome from other causes of amenorrhea. Used in infertility evaluation, puberty assessment, and pituitary function testing. Timing of sample collection is crucial for accurate interpretation.
